Today, there's a wedge being driven between black people and police in particular. Police feel threatened because of higher crime rates among black people and black communities. Black people feel threatened because police have lesser patience and tend to use more force or be more violent, and make more black arrests. It's a wedge that gets driven deeper and deeper and deeper with every situation like Sandra Bland or the teenagers. The days where police officers used to be seen as community protectors and members of a community are gone as that wedge has been driven harder and harder over the years. I feel like what we can do here on Voat is try to come to an understanding that not everything is as it seems. Hold officers and departments accountable, hold victims accountable, and try and promote a culture of understanding in times like this. I remember talking to an officer I know not long ago. I asked him how things have changed since these stories started to break and since injustices began happening in Baltimore or St. Louis or any of the other ones, I wanted an officer's opinion. As a small-city officer, he said, they had honestly felt threatened for the first time in a long time. It went from being the one-off traffic stop to being every other traffic stop that someone had to try and be hostile or yell or refuse to comply. On the flip side, because people got hostile, he had to get hostile too. The point of this is that I believe that this supports my thoughts of a wedge being driven between police and the community. Understanding and comunication can help restore relations to be what they should be: Peaceful and just. Body cams are incredible for this if they're unedited. They help hold officers accountable. Social media helps hold officers accountable. But I feel like the wrong response to this is outrage. As a community, we need to focus on harboring this understanding.

When I was younger and angrier, I lived in a town that was notorious for speed traps. I had just passed a speed trap set up at the bottom of a steep hill and looked over and saw the local police car parked there. I knew they liked to set up there, being a local, so I was under the speed limit when i passed him. Being particularly indignant that day for being targeted with this revenue generating scam, I threw up the middle finger as I passed. He pulled out behind me, so I consciously obeyed all traffic laws as I opened my sunroof and extended my hand with the previously mentioned middle finger out of it. He pulled me over. He walked up and asked if I was trying to say something. My response spoke in a reasonable manner, as I remember it was "I have a very low opinion of people who try and entrap people". I also asked, politely, why he pulled me over. He mentioned disturbing the peace as his reasoning (this was before the court decisions on this subject). I was about to start into my rebuttal when my girlfriend at the time reminded me of her presence in the car and that I had better immediately apologize. I apologized and he let me go.

I guess the moral of this story is to keep some minimal level of control over yourself at all times and bring a SO to pull you off the ledge if your stubborn.
